parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national layer with a strongly protective division. Universal exposure sits at the border: the Nov 2025-upheld passport marker regime, the Feb 2025 visa cable directing refusal on any sex discrepancy with a possible lifetime fraud bar, reported confiscations/strandings, and advisories from 8+ foreign governments. Federal buildings and federally funded facilities exclude trans people despite this division's absent bans and its 2014 pro-access ruling. Detention tails into documented federal custody abuse. Against this, the division operates real protections: full anti-discrimination coverage, easy marker changes, protected care, hate-crime enhancements, gender-identity prison placement, and functioning courts. Net: systematic administrative severity without criminalisation or documented visitor violence here.

entry_documents.exposure: National regime: X markers ended, M/F only per supporting documents (SCOTUS allowed Nov 2025); Feb 2025 visa cable orders refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and allows consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report confiscated/blocking passports and stranding; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories by Mar-Apr 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; ACLU suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ maintains guidance.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at adjudication can escalate to refusal, border detention, then federal immigration custody where trans detainees documented abuse; state protections do not reach the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Foreign nationals of a neighbouring jurisdiction detained over visa issues (prompting advisories). Federal corrections bureau adopted from 2026 conversion-therapy-style inmate policies (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of transgender men; trans prisoner counts unpublished since 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State corrections house a trans woman by gender identity (documented Apr 2026); state courts function for trans people; no documented visitor arrest in this division.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry-document refusal is the gateway into federal custody, which sits outside the division's protective corrections practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Jan 2025 executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationally, reaching federal buildings, airports and federally funded schools inside this division; nationwide map shows bans in 9+9+3 units and criminal triggers in 4 units.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no facility restriction; its high court ruled in 2014 for congruent bathroom access; it sits in the July 2026 assessment's low-risk group.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State tolerance does not cancel the federal facility rule in federally funded settings the visitor actually enters.

care_services.exposure: National EOs frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation,' freeze funding, and proposed rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 hospital records in 2025; national funding threats already produced this division's university sports capitulation.
care_services.protection: Division protects gender-affirming care (Apr 2024 law), allows hormones for 16-17s since Jul 2023, bans conversion therapy on minors (2019), mandates SOGI data in facilities from Oct 2026.
care_services.interaction: Federal funding leverage has demonstrably overridden division policy once; provider chilling for visiting minors is plausible but undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ Dec 2025 reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' in extremist context; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; advocates compare the record to early genocide stages; 2025 poll: 66% support sex-at-birth document laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same memo states gender ideology is not a reward criterion and CT powers will not target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute plus division enhancements; trans-panic defence abolished 2019.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing raises the severity of any police encounter even where division officers are bound by protective law.

minors_guardians.exposure: The national document regime applies equally to a child's passport; the Jan 2025 order criminalising facilitation of a trans minor's social transition and the 'mutilation' EO shape federal scrutiny of travelling families; federal facility ban covers government-funded schools.
minors_guardians.protection: Division bans conversion therapy on minors, protects their care, and has no facility restriction; no documented visitor-facing harm to a minor in this division.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent's document mismatch and any minor's emergency care fall under federal framing while division law protects.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Inventory explicitly lacks state-specific violence figures and hate-crime enforcement statistics; national bias statistics track sexual orientation, not gender identity; no visitor-targeted incident documented here.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Well-documented division with functioning institutions, upheld protections (2005, 2021), hate-crime enhancements and a 2014 pro-access ruling; silence here is mildly positive given the dense record.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and several EOs unresolved; SCOTUS let passport restrictions take effect; lifetime fraud findings have limited waiver; exposure varies by which measures are in force at travel time.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division courts have ruled for trans people (2014), protections survived two referenda, national courts enjoined several orders, legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border decisions are the least remedy-accessible stage; state courts cannot reach them.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A. Vellandra's register bars entry routinely with near-nil appeal. Here refusal requires a discrepancy or doubt finding, the fraud bar is never automatic, and the destination division affirmatively protects facilities, care and accommodation. No detention-and-removal regime exists in this division.

Closest structural match: discretionary border screening, administrative rather than criminal outcomes, humiliation, slow or ineffective remedies, high uncertainty. Rated slightly above because the division's operative protections (court-enforced access, anti-discrimination, protected care) are documented as working, though below it on the systematic, court-upheld document refusal.

Lower than 0.75-C. Meridia's border recognises markers, trains officers, and offers compensation for brief detention. Here the national regime affirmatively refuses markers and sex-discrepant applications, has generated foreign travel advisories, and feeds into custody settings with documented abuse.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two stacked systems. At the border the national document and visa regime operates as a near-universal exposure: presentation diverging from an M/F marker invites refusal, secondary scrutiny and a possible lifetime fraud finding, with a documented tail into federal detention where trans custody abuse is recorded. Inside the division, the operative experience is markedly safer — no facility crime, court-protected access, full anti-discrimination coverage, protected care and hate-crime enhancements — but it does not reach federal buildings, federal custody or visa adjudication. Federal hostile framing and pending litigation make exposure time-dependent. The rating sits mid-scale: systematic administrative severity and custody tails without criminalisation of identity, documented visitor violence, or a hostile division.
